criteria.name: required_server_backed_workspace
criteria.description:
From a signed-out page, sign in as `avery@dropline.test` with `password123`.
Require successful same-origin application requests and a protected workspace
that visibly identifies Avery and contains a game board, status, totals,
history, and game controls. A static imitation with no successful application
request does not pass. Do not start, reset, or play a game.
criteria.reasoning: In a fresh context, signed-out view showed only sign-in controls; no board or totals were visible. An incorrect password was rejected with “Invalid email or password.” Avery sign-in succeeded via local POST /api/login (200), followed by GET /api/game (200) carrying an Authorization: Bearer token. The workspace showed Avery’s identity, board, status, totals, history, and controls. No game state was mutated.

criteria.name: local_refresh_and_health
criteria.description:
While Avery's workspace is visible, fully reload the page and require the
authenticated workspace to render again and remain usable. Browser network
evidence must show game state being delivered by the local application;
public browser assets are permitted. A same-origin `GET /api/health` request
must also succeed. Do
not require any particular saved board, history, or totals.
criteria.reasoning: After a full reload, the authenticated workspace rendered again and remained usable. Network evidence showed local GET /api/game (200) with a bearer token, and GET /api/health (200) returned ok:true for DropLine. No fatal browser error or unresolved spinner was observed.

criteria.name: seeded_state_import_and_isolation
criteria.description:
Before any game mutation, sign in as Avery. Require visible identity Avery
Morgan and avery@dropline.test, revision 7, totals Red 2,
Yellow 1, Draws 1, Red at row 6 column 4, Yellow at row 6 column 5, every other
cell empty, `Red's turn`, two matching applied-history entries, Undo and Redo
available, and no completed match. Activate Redo and require the workbook's Red
move at row 5 column 4, three matching history entries, `Yellow's turn`, and
revision 8. Undo and require the original board, history, turn, totals, and Redo
availability restored at revision 9. Sign out, sign in as Jordan, and require
revision 4, totals Red 1, Yellow 2, Draws 0, Red at row 6 column 2, Yellow at
row 6 column 3, Red at row 5 column 2, `Yellow's turn`, three matching history
entries, Undo available, and Redo unavailable. Jordan's archive must show
an overall count of eleven and exactly the latest ten workbook
matches newest first, in this result/move-count order: Yellow/8, Red/7, Draw/42,
Yellow/8, Red/7, Draw/42, Yellow/8, Red/7, Draw/42, Yellow/8. The oldest
workbook Red/7 match must be omitted. Sign out and return to Avery; require
Avery's exact post-undo revision-9 state unchanged and no Jordan archive data.
criteria.reasoning: Gate passed; Avery and Jordan loaded with the required seeded revisions, boards, turns, totals, histories, and Jordan’s exact 10-of-11 archive window. Avery’s redo/undo returned to revision 9 unchanged.

criteria.name: completed_match_archive_and_replay
criteria.description:
Setup: use the shared Red-win journey in the prompt, recording the separate
history criterion's checkpoints during the same actions. As Avery, record the
displayed and overall Completed matches counts and totals, start New game, and
play 1,7,2,7,3,6,4. Require one new newest archive entry named `Red wins` with
seven moves. Open it, move Replay step to 7, and require a separate 42-cell
read-only replay board at step 7 of 7 showing the final position. Move Replay
step to 0 and require 42 empty replay cells; use Next once and require only Red
at replay row 6 column 1; return to step 7 and require the exact completed
position. Throughout replay, the active winning board, totals, history,
revision, and controls stay unchanged.

Undo the winning move and require active play, the score increment reversed,
and both archive counts reduced by one. Capture the history/markers checkpoint
and reload while undone for the shared history leg. Redo it and require the identical win
and exactly one restored archive entry in both counts, including its original completion ordering.
A repeated Redo attempt changes nothing. Reload and require the archive entry
and active terminal state to persist. Start New game and require the archive
entry to remain while active round state resets.
criteria.reasoning: Shared 1,7,2,7,3,6,4 win archived as Red wins/7; replay step 0/1/7 was exact, and undo, reload, redo, repeated redo, terminal reload, and New game preserved the required archive and active-state behavior.

criteria.name: gravity_turns_and_full_column
criteria.description:
Play columns 4,4,4. Require Red at row 6 column 4, Yellow at row 5 column 4,
Red at row 4 column 4, every other cell empty, `Yellow's turn`, and three
matching history entries. Start New game and click column 1 six times. Require
bottom-to-top Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow and `Red's turn`. Record all
cells, history, totals, revision, and archive; one more click must show
`Column 1 is full` without changing board, turn, history, Undo/Redo
availability, totals, revision, or archive.
Activate New game and require the full-column feedback to disappear.
criteria.reasoning: 4,4,4 produced correct gravity and turn state; six drops in column 1 filled bottom-to-top R/Y/R/Y/R/Y, and the seventh drop changed only the full-column feedback.

criteria.name: horizontal_and_vertical_wins
criteria.description:
Use the already captured Red win in the shared competitive journey; do not
play another horizontal match. Require `Red wins`, exactly row 6
columns 1-4 marked winning, seven history entries, and Red's total increased by
one from its own captured baseline. After that shared journey finishes,
record the current Red total, start New game, play 1,2,1,2,1,2,1, and require `Red wins`, exactly column
1 rows 3-6 marked winning, seven history entries, and Red's total increased by
one from this new baseline. Start New game and play 7,1,7,1,6,1,6,1. Require `Yellow wins`,
exactly column 1 rows 3-6 marked winning, and one Yellow score increment.
No other cell is winning in any game.
criteria.reasoning: The shared horizontal Red win marked exactly row 6 columns 1-4; subsequent Red and Yellow vertical games marked exactly column 1 rows 3-6 with independent score increments.

criteria.name: both_diagonal_wins
criteria.description:
Play 1,2,2,3,4,3,3,4,5,4,4. Require `Red wins` with exactly row 6 column 1,
row 5 column 2, row 4 column 3, and row 3 column 4 marked winning. Start New
game and play 7,6,6,5,4,5,5,4,3,4,4. Require the mirrored win at row 3 column
4, row 4 column 5, row 5 column 6, and row 6 column 7. Require eleven matching
history entries and no other winning cell in either game. Start New game and
play 7,1,2,2,3,4,3,3,4,5,4,4; require `Yellow wins` at row 6 column 1, row 5
column 2, row 4 column 3, and row 3 column 4. Start New game and play
1,7,6,6,5,4,5,5,4,3,4,4; require the mirrored Yellow diagonal and no other
winning cell.
criteria.reasoning: Both Red diagonal sequences and both mirrored Yellow sequences produced exactly the specified four winning cells, correct histories, and no extra markers.

criteria.name: yellow_win_and_terminal_lock
criteria.description:
Record Yellow's total and archive count, then play 7,1,7,2,6,3,6,4. Require `Yellow wins`, exactly
the four Yellow pieces at row 6 columns 1-4 marked winning, eight history
entries, Yellow's total increased by one, and one newest `Yellow wins` archive
entry with eight moves. Record board, result, markers,
history, totals, revision, and archive; attempt columns 5 and 1. Require every
recorded value to remain exactly unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: The eight-move Yellow win marked exactly row 6 columns 1-4, incremented Yellow and archive once, and later drops left board, result, history, totals, revision, and archive unchanged.

criteria.name: exact_draw_and_terminal_lock
criteria.description:
Record Draws and the archive count, then play exactly
4,4,4,4,4,4,3,3,3,3,3,3,5,2,5,6,5,5,5,5,2,2,2,2,2,6,1,6,6,6,6,1,1,1,1,1,7,7,7,7,7,7.
Require all 42 cells occupied, visible result exactly `Draw`, zero winning
markers, exactly 42 history entries, and Draws increased by one. Attempt one
later drop and require board, result, history, totals, and the single new newest
`Draw` archive entry with 42 moves unchanged, with no revision increment.
Undo the final drawing move: require active play, 41 occupied cells, Draws
returned to its baseline and that round removed from the archive. Redo must
restore the exact full draw board, one Draws increment and one archive record.
criteria.reasoning: The exact 42-move sequence filled all cells with Draw and zero markers; terminal drop was inert, Undo removed the draw, and Redo restored the exact full draw and archive record.

criteria.name: move_history_undo_redo_branching
criteria.description:
Start New game and play 4,5,4. Require the history to read, in order, Red at
column 4 row 6, Yellow at column 5 row 6, and Red at column 4 row 5. Undo twice.
Require only the first Red piece and first history entry to remain, status
`Yellow's turn`, Redo available, and exactly two revision increments. Reload
and require that exact revision and state. Redo once and require the Yellow
piece/history entry restored with `Red's turn`, another Redo still available,
one revision increment, and a distinct opaque high-entropy operation identifier
on every Undo and Redo request. Now play column 2. Require a new Red entry at
column 2 row 6, Redo unavailable, and one revision increment; a Redo attempt,
if the UI permits one, must change nothing.

For the terminal leg, use the SAME new match and captured checkpoints as
completed_match_archive_and_replay in the shared Red-win journey; do not
replay an already observed leg. Record Red's total before its 1,7,2,7,3,6,4.
Require the
Red win and one score increment. Undo once: require an active round with
`Red's turn`, the last Red piece and every winning marker removed, six history
entries, and the Red total returned to its baseline. Reload and require the
same undo state. Redo once: require the identical Red win, four markers, seven
history entries, and exactly one restored score increment. Redo is then
unavailable and cannot increment the score again.
criteria.reasoning: 4,5,4 history, two undos, reload, redo, branch move, stale redo, and the shared terminal undo/redo all matched the required positions, revisions, markers, and distinct operation IDs.

criteria.name: new_game_reset_and_persistence
criteria.description:
Before the shared competitive win journey, start New game, play column 4,
and Undo. Require Redo available. Record the
revision, activate New game, and require exactly one revision increment, all 42
cells empty, no history, and Redo unavailable. Use the shared journey's existing
Red win and its final New game after replay/Undo/Redo/reload; do not create
another win. Capture all three totals and the current revision immediately
before that final New game. Require exactly one revision increment, all 42 cells empty, no winning
markers, no history, Undo and Redo unavailable, status exactly `Red's turn`,
and recorded totals unchanged. Click column 7 and require Red at row 6 column 7,
one matching history entry, and `Yellow's turn`. Fully reload the page and
require that exact one-piece board, history, turn, totals, revision, and Undo
availability to remain. Network evidence must show every New game request used
a distinct opaque high-entropy operation identifier.
criteria.reasoning: New game after col4/undo cleared the board with one revision increment; the shared post-win reset preserved totals/archive, col7 and reload preserved the one-piece state, and New game IDs were distinct opaque values.

criteria.name: keyboard_focus_and_activation
criteria.description:
Start New game. Focus `Drop in column 1` without pointer navigation. Press
ArrowRight and require column 2 focus, End for column 7, Home for column 1,
ArrowLeft and require focus remains at column 1, then Right twice and Left once
for column 2. Press Enter and require Red at row 6 column 2 with focus still on
column 2. Press Space and require Yellow at row 5 column 2 with that focus still
usable and two matching history entries. Navigate to Undo and activate it by
keyboard; require the Yellow move removed and Redo enabled. Activate Redo by
keyboard and require the same Yellow move restored without losing usable focus.
criteria.reasoning: ArrowRight/End/Home/ArrowLeft navigation, Enter/Space drops, and keyboard Undo/Redo preserved the required focused columns, pieces, history, and usable focus.

criteria.name: multi_tab_revision_and_duplicate_guard
criteria.description:
In tab A, sign in as Avery and start New game. Open tab B, sign in as Avery,
and record the same empty board and visible revision in both tabs. In tab A,
capture the app's successful Red move request and drop Red in column 1. Replay
that exact same-origin request with the same body and bearer credential; require
the original successful response but no second piece, history entry, score,
archive entry, or revision increment. Without refreshing tab B, capture its
column 2 request and attempt it. Require visible `Game updated in another tab`,
the authoritative one-piece board and history from tab A, and no Yellow move or
extra revision. Retry column 2 through its visible control, which must use a new
identifier, and require one accepted Yellow move and one revision increment.
Now replay the original stale request after state has advanced; require its
original conflict response while a fresh game read still shows the two-move
state and current revision unchanged. Require every newly captured move request
to carry a distinct opaque high-entropy operation identifier. Then rapidly
double-activate column 3 while its first request is demonstrably pending. You
may delay delivery of that real server response without altering its body,
status or request so the pending interval is observable; do not count two
separate activations after the first response as a duplicate-pending defect.
Require exactly one
Red piece at row 6 column 3, exactly three total history entries, one revision
increment, and the same three-move state after reloading tab A.
criteria.reasoning: Separate Avery tabs showed the same revision; exact move replay was idempotent, stale tab conflict adopted authoritative state, retry used a new ID, stale replay remained rejected, and held-response double activation accepted one move only.

criteria.name: cross_tab_sign_out_revocation
criteria.description:
Submit the Avery login form separately in tabs A and B, and use network evidence
to require two distinct issued bearer tokens. Record the same board, history,
totals, archive, and revision, and capture tab B's actual protected game-read
request before signing out. Sign out in tab A and require its protected board
and totals to disappear. If tab B still shows its game,
attempt a visible action and require return to sign-in with no mutation.
Proactive automatic sign-out of tab B is also correct; do not demand a control
that has already disappeared. In either case replay the captured protected
read with tab B's old token and require rejection with no protected game data.
Sign in again in tab B and require every recorded game value unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: Independent login responses issued distinct tokens; sign-out revoked the other tab’s protected action and old read token, with no mutation, and re-login restored identical game data.

criteria.name: accessible_grid_and_winning_names
criteria.description:
Use the shared competitive journey's empty board before its Red win and the
same board immediately after that win. Do not play another match.
Confirm the empty active board exposes one grid
with exactly 42 grid cells and every cell name identifies its row, column, and
empty state.
Require exactly four winning Red cells; each accessible name must include its
row, column, Red, and winning, while no other cell name includes winning.
criteria.reasoning: The empty active board exposed one 42-cell grid with row/column/empty names; the shared win exposed exactly four Red winning names and no other winning cell names.

criteria.name: analysis_fork_exact_prefix
criteria.description:
Setup: open the Red source replay from the prompt at step 6; record the
competitive game and archive, then create a new named analysis.
1. Require one saved analysis with the chosen name, source identity, step 6,
revision 0 and one selected root. Its full six-move history is 1,7,2,7,3,6.
2. Require a separate 42-cell board: Red at row 6 columns 1,2,3; Yellow at
row 6 columns 6,7 and row 5 column 7; all other cells empty; Red to move,
active, no winning markers. Creation has not changed the competitive game.
3. Reload, reopen this analysis from its list and require the identical name,
source, root, six-move history, board and revision. Do not require auto-opening
the study on page load.
criteria.reasoning: The saved named analysis of the Red source at step 6 had revision 0, one root, exact six-move history and board, remained separate from competition, and reopened identically.

criteria.name: analysis_sibling_paths_and_navigation
criteria.description:
Setup: fresh Red-source analysis at step 6. Record its root identity.
1. Drop in analysis column 4 (child A), Undo to root, then drop in column 5
(child B). Require both distinct children visible under that root, three
total nodes, and B selected. Undo must not delete A.
2. Select A in the tree: require seven moves, Red win at row 6 columns 1-4.
Select B: require seven moves, Red at row 6 column 5, no Red at column 4,
active Yellow turn. Full histories must follow each selected branch.
3. Select root and explicitly choose A for Redo, then root and B for Redo.
Require each exact position. Select root and play column 5 again: require the
existing B identity, still three nodes, not a duplicate edge. Each accepted
selection/history/move action advances only the analysis revision by one.
criteria.reasoning: Correct shared study retained distinct root children A=[4] and B=[5], explicit redo selected each exact position, and replaying B reused its identity without duplication.

criteria.name: analysis_nested_continuations
criteria.description:
Setup: continue the shared branch journey after analysis_sibling_paths_and_navigation,
with B selected and A retained at the root. Play column 1 (C), Undo to B and
play column 2 (D). Do not create a second study or replay column 5.
1. Require root -> A and B, and B -> C and D, five nodes total; C and D are siblings
under B, not children of root. Their eight-move histories share seven moves.
2. Select C: Yellow is at row 5 column 1, row 5 column 2 empty, Red to move.
Select D: Yellow is at row 5 column 2, row 5 column 1 empty, Red to move.
The other seven pieces follow the source plus Red at row 6 column 5.
3. Rename through its labelled control, reload and reopen. Require the new
name, same five node identities and edges, selected D and its exact state.
criteria.reasoning: B’s continuations C=[5,1] and D=[5,2] formed siblings under B for five total nodes; both positions, rename, reload, reopen, and selected D were exact.

criteria.name: analysis_terminal_score_isolation
criteria.description:
Setup: fresh Red-source analysis at step 6; capture the entire competitive
game, totals, revision and archive as an isolation baseline.
1. Play analysis column 4. Require Red wins, seven applied moves and exactly
row 6 columns 1-4 marked winning. A later practice drop cannot change this
node. If terminal UI controls are disabled, that is valid UI locking.
2. Analysis Undo returns to the exact six-move active root with no winning
markers; Analysis Redo returns to that same terminal child identity.
3. Fresh competitive reads after the win, Undo and Redo must each equal the
isolation baseline. Practice must never award a score or archive a result.
criteria.reasoning: Analysis col4 produced the exact Red terminal child; analysis undo/redo restored the same node identity while competitive board, scores, archive, and revision remained byte-equivalent.

criteria.name: analysis_draw_and_root_boundary
criteria.description:
Setup: sign in as Jordan and open an existing 42-move Draw archive entry.
Create a fresh analysis at step 41 and record the competitive game. The seeded
Draw sequence is 4,4,4,4,4,4,3,3,3,3,3,3,5,2,5,6,5,5,5,5,2,2,2,2,2,6,1,6,6,6,6,1,1,1,1,1,7,7,7,7,7,7.
1. The root has 41 pieces, Yellow to move, only row 1 column 7 empty and no
winning cells. Undo is unavailable; it must not erase the source prefix.
2. Analysis column 7 makes a full Draw with 42 moves and zero winning cells.
Undo returns to the exact root, Redo restores the same full drawing node.
The competitive game, scores, archive and revision remain unchanged.
3. Reopen this match at step 42 and fork a second fresh analysis. Require a
terminal Draw root with no legal continuation and no parent to Undo to.
Return to Avery for later criteria. Use an existing matching seeded Draw;
do not assume it is the newest archive entry.
criteria.reasoning: Jordan’s step-41 Draw analysis had only column 7 legal, completed to Draw, undid/redid exactly, and step-42 reopened as a terminal root with no parent continuation.

criteria.name: analysis_position_comparison
criteria.description:
Setup: continue the shared branch journey after analysis_nested_continuations.
Use its existing A and C; do not create another study or replay their moves.
Capture the saved five-node study and competitive state before comparing.
1. Compare A and C through the labelled selectors. Require two complete
42-cell boards, common prefix 6, and exactly three differing cells: row 6
column 4, row 6 column 5 and row 5 column 1. A is the seven-move Red win;
C has Red at row 6 column 5 and Yellow at row 5 column 1 instead.
2. Each differing cell has a visible non-color-only indication and accessible
difference wording; all cells name coordinates/occupants and winning status.
3. Swap sides: boards swap and the same three differences remain. Compare C
with itself: prefix 8 and no differences. Fresh saved-study and competitive
reads after comparisons equal their baselines, including selected cursor.
criteria.reasoning: A versus C showed common prefix 6 and exactly three coordinate differences with accessible wording; side swap preserved them, C versus itself showed prefix 8/no differences, and saved state stayed unchanged.

criteria.name: analysis_ownership_boundaries
criteria.description:
Setup: create two fresh Avery studies from Red source step 6 and record IDs
and roots. Sign in separately as Jordan. Server probes using captured actual
analysis and login requests are permitted for this criterion.
1. Jordan's list excludes both studies. Reading or editing an Avery study,
forking Avery's source match, or comparing its nodes using Jordan's bearer
token must return a controlled 4xx without any protected Avery study data.
2. Using Avery's token, try to select, redo or compare a node from the second
study in the first. Each is rejected and both studies remain exactly unchanged.
If comparison is entirely client-side, require its selectors contain only
nodes of the open study; server selection/redo rejection is still mandatory.
3. Capture a Jordan protected study-list read, sign Jordan out in another
independently signed-in tab and retry that read: require authentication
rejection and no studies. Sign back in; saved studies are not deleted.
criteria.reasoning: Jordan could not list/read/edit/fork/compare Avery studies; Avery cross-study node operations were rejected atomically, and Jordan’s revoked list read was rejected before identical re-login recovery.

criteria.name: analysis_stale_edit_and_recovery
criteria.description:
Setup: open one fresh Avery Red-source step-6 study in two signed-in tabs,
both at its root and revision 0.
1. In A play analysis column 5. In unrefreshed B try column 4. Require a
visible stale-analysis conflict and adoption of A's two-node study, without
a new branch or revision increment. Capture B's stale request for the next
criterion's type of retry observation only if useful; do not assume a URL.
2. Retry a legal analysis column 1 in B through the UI with a new operation
identifier. Require one Yellow piece at row 5 column 1, three nodes total,
revision 2. Reload A and reopen: require that exact tree and selection.
criteria.reasoning: Unrefreshed tab B received the visible stale-analysis conflict and adopted A’s branch; B’s new column 1 action used a new ID and produced the exact three-node revision-2 study after reload.

criteria.name: analysis_operation_receipts
criteria.description:
Setup: fresh Avery Red-source step-6 study. Capture its actual creation
request/response and successful UI move in column 5. Controlled same-origin
replays and metadata edits to observed requests are permitted here.
1. Replay the exact creation and accepted move after later selecting the
root. Require each original response/status and no duplicate study, node,
revision or cursor change in a fresh read. Newly intended UI actions must
use distinct opaque high-entropy identifiers.
2. Send a stale edit with a new valid identifier and old revision. Capture
its 409 response. Make one legal UI move, then replay the exact rejected
request: require the original conflict response, with fresh current state
unchanged. Reuse an accepted identifier with a different column: require 409
and no change, not a stale success response for different input.
3. In an active position, use the prompt's pending-repeat protocol for the same
analysis drop. Capture before-revision/node count, first request, second physical
activation while its response is held, then release and capture after-state.
Require one accepted node/revision, not two moves. Keep this evidence separate
from exact receipt replay in steps 1-2. An actionability wait that postpones the
second click until the response completes is not a valid pending-repeat test.
criteria.reasoning: Exact creation and move receipt replays returned original responses without duplicates; stale and reused-ID edits returned 409 unchanged, and held-response pending repeat accepted one analysis move.

criteria.name: analysis_rejections_are_atomic
criteria.description:
Setup: fresh Red-source analysis at step 0; capture real creation/edit/read
requests. Controlled invalid-input probes against those actual routes are
permitted. Compare fresh saved state before/after each rejection.
1. Probe creation with a blank and 61-character name; source steps -1, 0.5
and one past the source length; and a submitted board/account field. Require
controlled 4xx and no created study. Also fork step 0 with a whitespace-padded
valid name: require its trimmed name and empty Red-to-move root.
2. Probe edits with missing and malformed operation identifiers; missing,
string and fractional expected revisions; columns 0,8,1.5 and string '2';
unknown action; extra account/board fields; blank and 61-character rename.
Require controlled 4xx, never 500, and no node/cursor/revision/name changes.
3. At the root reject Undo and Redo without a child. Through UI play column
1 six times; a seventh is rejected without change. Create two children of
the root and probe Redo without a child choice: require conflict. Finally
select the root and play analysis columns 1,7,2,7,3,6,4 (reopening an existing
first child is valid). At the resulting Red win probe another drop: require conflict
without change. Use supported UI setup; do not inject positions.
criteria.reasoning: Invalid creation and edit matrices returned controlled 400s, root undo/redo and ambiguous redo returned controlled conflicts, full columns and terminal moves were rejected without state changes.

criteria.name: analysis_source_snapshot_independence
criteria.description:
Setup: run after the other new analysis criteria. Create a fresh competitive
Red win (New game, 1,7,2,7,3,6,4), fork step 6, add practice column 5 and
record its full study with source metadata and selected child.
1. Undo the competitive winning move so that source archive entry disappears.
Reopen the study: require the unchanged frozen source and exact tree/state.
2. Start a new competitive game, reload and reopen the study again. Require
the same study, then add a legal practice column 1. Require the expected
Yellow piece at row 5 column 1 while that new competitive game stays empty.
criteria.reasoning: After undoing the competitive source win and starting a new competitive game, the frozen study and its practice continuation reopened unchanged and practice did not mutate the empty competitive round.

criteria.name: restart_persistence_and_seed_idempotence
criteria.description:
Run this last, after all other Functional criteria. Follow checkpoints R0-R4
in order; the game Redo belongs BETWEEN the two restarts, not after both.
R0. Through the visible UI,
sign in as Avery, start New game, play columns 4,5,4 and Undo once. Capture a
fresh server-backed record of board, turn/result, winning cells, totals,
applied history, redo availability, revision and completed matches.
R1. Restart
the application with bash /tests/app-lifecycle.sh restart, then reload and
sign in again if required. Require every captured game value and archive
record unchanged.
R2. Activate game Redo through the UI NOW. Require it restores the third move
exactly and advances the revision once. Capture this new game and archive.
R3. Repeat restart
and require that R2 post-Redo state and archive unchanged, with no duplicate
completed matches or replacement of the captured account state. Do not infer persistence from a browser
reload alone. A browser-tool disconnection is unverified evidence, not proof
that the app lost data; do not invent successful post-restart reads.

Before the first restart, also snapshot both accounts' full study lists and
each study's name, frozen source, all node identities/edges/positions, selected
cursor and revision. Record one completed analysis operation's request and
response. After each of the same two restarts, reopen the saved studies and
require those exact snapshots unchanged, with no duplicate studies or nodes.
Replay the recorded operation after the second restart: its original response
must return while a fresh study read stays unchanged. Use captured legitimate
analysis requests for this receipt observation; do not add a third restart.
Also retain successful and rejected transplant receipts plus one tactical
report before restarting. After the same two restarts, exact receipt retries

match. Do not play, reset or change the active game. Require the replay to be

unchanged active board, revision, totals and history. Do not demand that the

Replay announced result/step, exposed 42 named cells, tracked 0→1→8 occupied cells, supported keyboard slider/navigation, disabled endpoint controls, and Close restored revision 4, totals 1/2/0, and three history rows.

criteria.description:

Jordan replay and your own analysis tree/history/comparison must fit without horizontal page overflow, clipped controls or

totals, history, Undo, Redo, New game, archive and Sign out must be reachable
through ordinary vertical scrolling, as must analysis names, branch controls
and comparison selectors, plus transplant fields/preview and tactical tables,

fold or fixed panel placement. Inspect only: do not mutate the active game.
criteria.reasoning: At 375×760, document and body widths were 375 with no out-of-bounds elements. Sign-in, workspace, replay, analysis/comparison, transplant preview, tactical board, and proof nodes stacked within the viewport and were reachable by vertical scrolling.

controls, including transplant and tactical depth/report/proof controls.

Undo or Redo: exact game actions are graded by Functional, not here.

Release announced an unsaved preview. Keyboard Commit announced “Transplant committed…”, disabled Commit, and left focus on enabled Refresh destinations.

criteria.name: analysis_keyboard_actions_and_feedback
criteria.description:
Setup: use your own practice study, selected at its empty root. Keyboard
actions here concern usability; exact branch data is graded by Functional.
1. Focus analysis column 1. Left stays there, End reaches 7, Home reaches 1,
Right reaches 2. Enter then Space activate two drops with useful visible focus
remaining on column 2. Wait for each completed response before the next.
2. Reach Analysis Undo and Redo by keyboard and activate each. Require usable
focus after completion, visible non-color-only saved feedback and an announced
status region. After Redo becomes unavailable, focus on another useful enabled
control is valid; do not insist on focus remaining on a disabled button.
3. Navigate to the variation tree and comparison selectors with Tab/Shift+Tab
and keyboard-select a position and compare. Require reachable, labelled
controls and no keyboard trap. Do not grade exact comparison arithmetic here.
criteria.reasoning: At the own study root, ArrowLeft/End/Home/ArrowRight produced 1/7/1/2; settled Enter and Space drops retained focus on column 2. Keyboard Tab reached Analysis Undo and Redo; each action announced “Analysis saved”, focus remained useful, and Redo became disabled. Tab/Shift+Tab reached both comparison selectors and Enter activated Compare.

criteria.name: page_load_and_refresh
criteria.description:
Open the same-origin page and require a substantive DropLine sign-in screen
with visible email and password fields and a usable sign-in control. Fully
refresh once and require the same usable page to render again
without a blank screen, fatal error, or broken layout that blocks the form.
criteria.reasoning: DropLine rendered a substantive sign-in screen with visible email and password fields and a usable Sign in button. After a full refresh, the same form rendered again with no blank screen, fatal error, unresolved spinner, or blocking layout issue.

render.judge_output: {"score":"yes","reasoning":"DropLine rendered a substantive sign-in screen with visible email and password fields and a usable Sign in button. After a full refresh, the same form rendered again with no blank screen, fatal error, unresolved spinner, or blocking layout issue."}

criteria.name: visual_typography
criteria.description:
Assess rendered sign-in, game, replay and populated analysis/comparison typography at desktop size.
5: deliberate, readable type sizes and weights distinguish product title,
account, turn/result, totals and secondary history; alignment is consistent.
4: readable with one or two minor sizing or alignment imperfections.
3: noticeable inconsistent sizing, crowding or awkward text truncation.
2: several important labels or history entries are difficult to read.
1: broadly illegible, misaligned or undifferentiated text.
0: no coherent typographic rendering on the reviewed surfaces.
Do not grade move correctness or exact seed values here.
criteria.reasoning: Readable, deliberate type scale across sign-in, game, replay, analysis titles, statuses, totals, history, tree, tables, and controls; emphasis and alignment remain consistent.

criteria.name: visual_color_and_contrast
criteria.description:
Assess the supplied theme; a theme switcher is not required.
5: cohesive palette with clearly distinguishable Red/Yellow pieces, empty
cells, legible text and purposeful accents across game, replay and analysis.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: some low-contrast text or conflicting accents distract from the board.
2: substantial legibility or piece-distinction problems.
1: widespread low contrast or harsh, incoherent color treatment.
0: no readable color treatment renders.
Judge appearance, not actual winner detection or accessible-name behavior.
criteria.reasoning: Cohesive dark/blue theme with highly distinguishable red and yellow pieces, dark empty cells, bright controls, and legible text across all inspected panels.

criteria.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
criteria.description:
Assess spacing on desktop sign-in, active board/history, replay and analysis tree/comparison.
5: consistent margins and alignment, deliberate board/control grouping and
balanced spacing between totals, history and replay.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several crowded, drifting or excessively separated elements.
2: frequent collisions, clipping or inconsistent gutters.
1: broadly unbalanced or broken layout.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders.
Do not require a specific arrangement or the reference's pixels.
criteria.reasoning: Strong grouping and consistent gutters on game, replay, comparison, transplant, and tactical panels. Minor imbalance remains in the wide completed-matches card and the very tall analysis workspace.

criteria.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
criteria.description:
Assess how easily the board, turn/result, account, totals, history and selected analysis can be
visually located on desktop without reading all surrounding text.
5: clear visual order with primary game state prominent and related secondary
information grouped; replay is clearly distinct from the active game.
4: mostly clear with minor competing emphasis.
3: several competing sections or important information visually buried.
2: headings, controls and content are difficult to distinguish.
1: little usable visual order.
0: no scannable hierarchy renders.
Functional correctness and keyboard traversal are outside this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Turn/status and board are immediately prominent; totals, history, replay, selected analysis, variation tree, comparison, preview, table, and proof board are clearly sectioned.

criteria.name: visual_overall_craft
criteria.description:
Assess visual consistency across sign-in, the game, replay and analysis/comparison.
5: one deliberate component language, integrated board-game identity and
finished treatment of history, empty states and secondary controls.
4: one or two minor inconsistent details.
3: noticeable default styling or inconsistent components between surfaces.
2: much of the interface looks unfinished or disconnected.
1: little considered component styling.
0: no crafted presentation renders.
Do not require branding, decorative assets or features absent from the brief.
criteria.reasoning: A consistent component language carries from sign-in through active game, replay, saved analysis, sibling branches, comparison, transplant preview, and tactical explanation, with polished cards, controls, boards, and messages.

criteria.name: visual_responsive_consistency
criteria.description:
Compare screenshots at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 760 for sign-in, game, replay and analysis/comparison.
5: typography, palette, component styling and hierarchy remain visually
coherent while the layout adapts naturally to each viewport.
4: minor visual inconsistency at one size.
3: visible uneven scaling, crowding or loss of hierarchy between sizes.
2: substantial visual fragmentation at the narrow size.
1: barely coherent presentation at one size.
0: no reviewable presentation at either size.
Score visual adaptation only; control reachability/overflow is graded by
Polish. Ordinary vertical scrolling is allowed; missing required surfaces
are not waived or treated as full-credit evidence.
criteria.reasoning: At 375px the game, totals, history, replay, analysis tree, comparison boards, preview, tables, and proof board stack naturally while preserving the same palette, typography, controls, and hierarchy; wrapping is controlled and no visual fragmentation was observed.
